Aujourd’hui, chacun fait ses choix. Et vos choix ont du pouvoir. 🌾 Consommer français, ce n’est pas un détail, c’est vital pour nos fermes. Comme disait Coluche : “il suffirait de ne pas acheter pour que ça ne se vende pas.” C’est simple. C’est puissant. Oui, nous traversons une crise agricole. Oui, les décisions politiques nous impactent. Mais au final, c’est vous qui décidez. Vous êtes ceux qui pouvez faire vivre notre agriculture. Manger français, c’est soutenir nos terres, nos métiers, nos valeurs. Pensez-y quand vous faites vos courses. Pensez-y pour vos enfants. Pensez-y pour l’avenir.   Et rappelez-vous : si on ne les achète pas, ça ne se vendra pas. #agricultura #agricultrice #loveyou #france🇫🇷 #paysanne

Il y a un mélange de tristesse, un peu de colère aussi, mais surtout un vrai merci. Merci pour ce que vous partagez, pour ce que vous transmettez. Ça compte plus que vous ne le pensez. J’ai découvert les cosmétiques Mademoiselle Agathe. Des soins 100% naturels, certifiés bio, et surtout… inspirés par la nature elle-même. Chaque crème, sérum, élixir ou savon est le fruit d’un savoir-faire français unique, qui valorise les bienfaits exceptionnels de la bave d’escargot 🐌. Une matière précieuse, régénérante et douce, qui reflète mes propres valeurs : respect, authenticité et amour du vivant. Je m’identifie pleinement à cette marque engagée, car comme dans ma ferme, la qualité et la pureté sont au cœur de tout. 🌿 Des ingrédients bio 🇫🇷 Une fabrication française 💧 Des résultats visibles et naturels Merci pour tout @Mademoiselle Agathe

🐔 Poulet local VS poulet amélioré : faut-il vraiment choisir ? On oppose souvent les deux… alors qu’ils ne répondent pas toujours aux mêmes objectifs. Le poulet local a ses forces : rusticité, adaptation au climat, goût apprécié. Les races améliorées répondent à un autre besoin : produire plus d’œufs et de viande pour une demande urbaine grandissante. La vraie question est peut-être ailleurs : 👉 Comment améliorer notre poulet local ? 👉 Comment mieux adapter les systèmes modernes à nos réalités ? 👉 Et surtout, comment utiliser davantage la recherche pour construire un élevage plus performant et durable ? À mon avis, le Burkina Faso n’a pas besoin de choisir entre les deux. Il a besoin d’intelligence, d’innovation… et de complémentarité. Et vous, vous êtes plutôt : 🐓 Poulet local ? 🐔 Poulet amélioré ? 🤝 Ou une combinaison des deux ? Je vous lis 👇🏽 #agrogirl #poulet #learning #viralvideos #Agriculture

Over the last four years I’ve been creating farming content and have enjoyed showing everyone behind the scenes of how agriculture works! I’ve tried to keep my private life out of social media, but this feels like a new chapter of my life, and I’m so excited to start showing more about my personal life. Most Americans today are 3–4 generations removed from the farm. That means for many people, the last person in their family who raised livestock, planted crops, or depended on the weather for their livelihood was their great-grandparent. When you’re that far removed from something, it stops being real. It becomes abstract. Food becomes something that comes from a store shelf, not from soil. Milk comes from a gallon jug, not from a cow. Corn becomes an ingredient, not a plant that fought wind, heat, insects, and time just to exist. This generational gap has created a divide. Not out of bad intent, but out of distance. When people don’t see agriculture firsthand, misconceptions fill the space where understanding should be. Assumptions replace experience. Narratives replace reality. But the truth is simple. Every day, there are people whose entire lives revolve around producing food. Early mornings. Late nights. Risk with no guarantees. All to feed people they will never meet. Agriculture isn’t just an industry. It’s a responsibility carried forward by fewer and fewer families with each generation. The farther removed we become, the more important it is to reconnect the story of food to the people and the work behind it. Because food doesn’t start at the store. It starts with someone willing to bet their life on a seed.

The Kgodiso Development Fund hosted a business breakfast to present its 2024/2025 Integrated Report, reflecting on four years of measurable impact in advancing inclusive growth in agriculture. Speaking to #FarmersWeeklySA, Diale Tilo, executive director of KDF said the fund had supported 96 small- and medium-scale farmers during the year under review. Tilo said the fund’s approach goes beyond finance by combining funding with mentorship, technical support and market access opportunities to help farmers build sustainable businesses and participate across the agricultural value chain. “Finance without support can become debt. Finance combined with mentorship becomes transformation,” he said. Watch the video as Tilo shares highlights from the event and speaks about the fund’s support for farmers. #farmingsouthafrica  #agfinance  #agriculturetiktok

Tai siis, ihan kohta mennään.. ensin pitää hoitaa viljelijän konetöitä, tietokonetöitä.  Viljelysuunnittelu on se, jolla päätetään mitä kylvetään, minne kylvetään ja millä toimenpiteillä. Mulla kun on 4-vuotista heinää mukana viljelykierrossa, suunnittelen aina seuraavat 6 vuotta pellolla kasvavien kasvien kiertoa. Nyt oon mukana Fazerin Viljelyohjelmassa, joka sisältää tavallisen viljavuustutkimuksen lisäksi vielä tarkemman NIR-analyysin. Niissä siis molemmissa laitetaan maata voipurkkiin, analysoidaan laboratoriossa ja sitte tiedetään, mitä pellon maa pitää sisällään ja mitä se kaipaa voidakseen hyvin! Chọn cành bánh tẻ (không quá già/non), cắm sâu 2/3 thân xuống đất, giữ ẩm cao. Sau 7-10 ngày cành ra rễ và phát triển nhanh, có thể thu hoạch sau khoảng 1 tháng. 1. Chuẩn bịCành giống: Chọn cành rau răm tươi, khỏe mạnh, không sâu bệnh từ chợ. Nên chọn cành có sẵn rễ ở các mắt (nếu có).Đất trồng: Rau răm ưa đất ẩm, tơi xốp, nhiều dinh dưỡng. Có thể dùng đất sạch trộn phân hữu cơ (phân trùn quế) hoặc đất vườn.Chậu/Thùng xốp: Có lỗ thoát nước tốt, hoặc trồng trực tiếp nơi đất ẩm, ít nắng (nơi ẩm ướt). 2. Các bước trồng (Giâm cành) Bước 1 - Xử lý cành: Ngắt bỏ bớt lá ở phía gốc, chỉ để lại 3-4 lá trên ngọn. Cắt cành dài khoảng 10-15cm.Bước 2 - Cắm cành: Cắm cành nghiêng 45 độ xuống đất, độ sâu khoảng 2/3 cành.Bước 3 - Khoảng cách: Cắm cách nhau khoảng 10-15cm để cây lan rộng.Bước 4 - Chăm sóc ban đầu: Tưới nước giữ ẩm ngay sau khi trồng. Đặt chậu vào nơi thoáng mát, ánh sáng yếu. 3. Chăm sóc và Thu hoạch Tưới nước: Rau răm cực kỳ ưa nước. Tưới 1-2 lần/ngày (sáng/chiều) để đất luôn ẩm.Bón phân: Sau khoảng 15-20 ngày, khi cây bén rễ, có thể bón phân hữu cơ hoặc NPK pha loãng để cây phát triển nhanh.Thu hoạch: Sau khoảng 30-45 ngày, có thể cắt ngọn để ăn, cây sẽ tiếp tục đẻ nhánh mới. Mẹo nhỏ: Bạn có thể ngâm cành rau răm vào cốc nước khoảng 3-5 ngày cho ra rễ trước khi đem cắm xuống đất để đảm bảo tỷ lệ sống cao hơn.  #rauram #cách_trồng_rau_răm #trồng_rau_răm  #rau_răm #1_5_hmhn

It is the vision of Dan Buettner who, with a team of expert demographers, identified four of the five blue zones hotspots and has led and aggregated the research to identify the common denominators. Gianni Pes first used the term "blue zone" to describe an area of extraordinary longevity in Sardinia’s Nuoro region. Pes, Michel Poulain, and Buettner are Blue Zones co-founders and continue to collaborate to identify, certify, and learn from blue zones hotspots around the world.

Hon. Minister was out of the country  with Mr President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at that time of the incident. He returned to Country today and stressed went to maiduguri visited the victims receiving treatment at the hospital . During the visit hon. Minister extended his support to the victims of the bomb explosions through cash assistance and also showed compassion to other patients in the ward. He prayed for their speedy recovery and called on Almighty Allah to bring a lasting end to insecurity in Borno State and Nigeria at large. Hon. Minister Abu kyari CON. also expressed his appreciation to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Vice President Kashim Shattima, and the Executive Governor of Borno State, His Excellency Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, for their continued support to the people of Borno State and their sustained efforts toward ending insecurity in the state and the nation. He further commended the Chief of Army Staff, ieutenant General Waidi Shaibu , for the military’s commitment and support in restoring peace and stability. 🚨 Saving lives cannot wait. Farmers, herders, and fishers — the people who feed us — are often the most vulnerable in crisis. Yet even in the harshest conditions, they keep going. Today, 295 million people face acute hunger. Among them, 87 million are in extreme conditions, where lives hang in the balance. The reality is simple: timely, practical agricultural support works. Seeds. Animal feed. Basic tools. These are not small inputs — they are lifelines. @fao is part of the global @un.ocha #87MillionLives campaign, calling on governments and partners to match the scale of the crisis. If there was ever a moment to act, it is now.

Forests need water. Water needs forests. And we need both! Forests power economies, while water drives inclusion and resilience. Yet access is not equal. Promoting gender equality and managing forests and water sustainably is key to a better future for all. #ForestDay #WorldWaterDay

@fao has published a new information note examining the potential implications of the escalating conflict in the Middle East for global agrifood systems. The analysis explores how disruptions to energy markets, fertilizer supply chains and key trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz could affect agricultural production costs, food prices and food security, particularly in import-dependent countries. In the latest special episode of the FAO podcast The Work We Do, Máximo Torero and David Laborde discuss how these shocks transmit through agrifood systems and what actions can help reduce risks. 🎧 Listen to the podcast episode and read the information note 👉 LINK IN BIO

School meals provide an essential source of daily nutrition for many children. In Bhutan, @FAO's One-Child, One-Egg initiative is helping make those meals more nutritious by adding one egg a day to school feeding programmes. Starting with 343 pilot schools and around 32 000 students, the initiative aims to improve children’s access to protein and micronutrients while also supporting local farmers and more sustainable agrifood systems. On International School Meals Day, this is a reminder that small additions can make a big difference. #SchoolMeals #ISMD2026 #MySchoolFood

Rising oil prices and growing inflation concerns are driving global bond yields to multi-year highs, increasing pressure on central banks ahead of critical interest rate decisions. According to market analysts, the ongoing geopolitical tensions involving the United States, Israel, and Iran have intensified fears that energy prices could remain elevated for an extended period. Brent crude prices trading above $100 per barrel have fueled expectations of persistent inflation, leading investors to demand higher yields on government bonds. Bond yields in major developed economies, including the United States, Japan, and the United Kingdom, have climbed sharply in recent weeks. The trend has also spread to emerging markets such as Türkiye, where local government bond yields have approached historic highs. Türkiye’s benchmark 10-year government bond yield reportedly rose to 35.85%, while five-year and two-year benchmark yields climbed to 39.52% and 43.74%, respectively. Analysts said the market is increasingly pricing in inflation risks and the possibility that the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (TCMB) could be forced to raise interest rates in June. Market participants also warned that prolonged geopolitical instability could push oil prices even higher, potentially reaching levels that would significantly worsen global inflation expectations. Analysts noted that investors are now assuming the U.S. Federal Reserve may avoid interest rate cuts this year and could even consider tighter policy in 2027 if inflationary pressures persist.

Dubai’s flagship travel trade event, Arabian Travel Market (ATM) 2026, has been moved to new dates, with organisers confirming that the show will now take place from September 14 to 17 at Dubai World Trade Centre. The date change comes after what organisers described as extensive consultation with exhibitors and industry stakeholders, with the move aimed at ensuring stronger participation from global travel businesses and buyers. The shift comes at a time when parts of the UAE’s events calendar have already seen disruption this year, with several concerts, exhibitions and industry gatherings either postponed or rescheduled as regional tensions affected flights, logistics and travel plans across the Gulf. ATM, which usually takes place April-May, itself had earlier been moved as organisers worked around industry disruption and participation concerns. Danielle Curtis, Regional Portfolio Director – UAE, RX Global, said: “We have been listening and working closely with our exhibitors, partners and stakeholders from across the global travel industry, and the decision to move Arabian Travel Market 2026 to 14–17 September reflects that ongoing dialogue and collaboration.” She added: “Our priority is always to ensure that ATM delivers the strongest possible platform for business, networking and partnership opportunities for the international travel community.”

Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz emphasized the government’s commitment to reducing inflation while maintaining sustainable economic growth, stating that the country’s economic program continues to produce positive results. Speaking during a televised interview and at various economic meetings, Yılmaz said Türkiye expects a more favorable financial outlook in 2026, with inflation continuing to decline and growth remaining stable. He noted that the government’s disinflation strategy is being supported by selective policies aimed at protecting key industries and employment. Yılmaz stated that sectors such as textiles, leather, furniture, and agriculture are receiving targeted support to minimize the impact of tight monetary policies. He added that exporters are benefiting from lower-cost financing compared with general market rates. The vice president also stressed that Türkiye’s economy has demonstrated resilience despite global economic uncertainty, pandemics, earthquakes, and inflationary pressures. According to Yılmaz, the Turkish economy grew by around 30% between 2020 and 2024, compared with approximately 15% growth in the global economy during the same period. Addressing inflation, Yılmaz said the government expects annual inflation to fall below 20% by the end of 2026. He pointed to measures targeting rental prices, private school fees, and food inflation as part of broader efforts to stabilize prices.

Amazon announced the general availability of the AWS Local Zone in Istanbul, Turkiye. The new AWS Local Zone in Istanbul brings AWS computing, networking, and local storage capabilities to Turkiye, helping end-users securely store and process data within the country while reducing latency. In 2019, AWS launched its first Local Zone in Los Angeles, making Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes available with single-digit millisecond latency. Today, AWS Local Zones operate in more than 30 metropolitan areas worldwide, helping customers meet their data placement requirements and run applications in more locations around the world.  The Istanbul Local Zone goes a step further by bringing Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), which helps you store, process, and retrieve objects locally, and Amazon EBS Snapshots for fast, on-premises backup and recovery, directly to Turkey.  This means Amazon S3 and Amazon EBS Snapshots are now available for the first time in AWS Local Zones across EMEA, opening up new possibilities for customers in Turkiye. The company stated: A new milestone in our decade-long investment: Istanbul Local Zone Since opening our first office in Turkiye in 2015, we have been steadily expanding our infrastructure in Turkiye to better serve our Turkish customers: In January 2024, AWS launched AWS Outposts in Turkiye, helping you extend AWS infrastructure and services to your on-premises or edge locations for a consistent hybrid experience. In February 2024, AWS launched an Amazon CloudFront edge location in Istanbul, providing Turkish users with up to 30% improvement in latency and performance in content delivery.  In May 2025, AWS launched the AWS Direct Connect location in Istanbul, helping you establish private, dedicated network connections between your on-premises infrastructure and AWS with 10 Gbps and 100 Gbps connections with MACsec encryption. The launch of the Istanbul Local Zone builds upon this foundation and strengthens our commitment to helping Turkish businesses, startups, and government agencies innovate and scale. Türkiye has moved several health report procedures to digital platforms under a new regulation, allowing citizens to obtain certain medical documents online through the country’s e-Nabız health care platform without visiting a hospital. The new regulation, published in the Official Gazette, aims to accelerate the country’s medical reporting procedures by moving applications and approvals to a digital format. Under the new system, written petitions for health reports will be abolished, and all applications will be submitted electronically. Citizens participating in non-licensed sports and social activities can now obtain a health certificate directly through e-Nabız, provided they self-declare that they have no medical issues. The regulation also expands the authority to issue pre-employment health reports for low-risk workplaces with fewer than 50 employees. Such reports can now be prepared by all public-sector physicians, a move intended to reduce congestion in the healthcare system.

Education costs continue to burden UAE households, with 88% of parents reporting financial strain when school fees are due, according to a survey by a financial services app. The study by Tabby, based on responses from 2,814 parents, found that half struggle to pay fees upfront in a single instalment. Nine in ten said flexible payment options would help their children take part in more activities by allowing costs to be broken into monthly instalments. Tabby has announced a deeper push into the education sector through a partnership with school fee platform Zenda. The aim is to make tuition and other education-related costs more manageable through structured instalment plans. Families can spread payments for tuition, transport, extracurricular activities, and other school expenses over up to 12 months. The companies highlight that there are no hidden fees. The survey also showed a strong appetite for such solutions, with 97 per cent of parents indicating they would likely use a school-offered flexible payment option. Tabby says it is already working with more than 100 educational institutions across the UAE, including schools such as Amity School Dubai, Sharjah University, other varsities, nurseries, and professional training centres.

The legendary Orient Express is set to launch its iconic Rome-to-Istanbul route this autumn, offering travelers a five-day luxury rail journey across Europe with ticket prices starting at 20,000 euros. The new service, operated under the name La Dolce Vita Orient Express, is scheduled to depart on Oct. 22 from Rome, retracing one of the continent’s most celebrated railway routes while blending nostalgia, haute cuisine and old-world elegance. Passengers will begin their journey at Rome’s Ostiense Station, where they will be welcomed inside the newly designed Orient Express Lounge created by architect Hugo Toro. Guests will be treated to sparkling drinks, aperitivo-style cuisine and live Italian music before boarding the train in the evening. The train’s interiors draw inspiration from 1960s Italy, featuring lavish suites and cabins designed to evoke the golden age of European rail travel. Travelers dining aboard the train will sample menus curated by three-Michelin-starred chef Heinz Beck. During the journey, the train will make stops in some of Europe’s most historic cities. After departing Rome, passengers will arrive in Venice before continuing to Budapest. The route then crosses the Carpathian Mountains into Romania, stopping in the medieval city of Braşov and the mountain resort town of Sinaia. ⭐️ WELCOME TO MY NEW SERIES: Educational Mini Comics all about INSECT AGRICULTURE 🎓 Topic: Entomophagy vs. Insectivory Fun fact! There are two scientific words for insect eating: insectivory and entomophagy. But they don’t mean exactly the same thing! 🪲 Insectivory = eating mainly insects (like anteaters or frogs). 🍽️ Entomophagy = humans eating insects occasionally or supplementally. So if you enjoy a crunchy cricket snack sometimes, you’re not an insectivore, you’re an entomophage! ‘Phagy’ means to eat, but it’s often used for unusual or rare behaviors, like: 🪨 Geophagy = eating dirt 💩 Coprophagy = eating poop* 😬 That makes ‘entomophagy’ sound weird or abnormal, even though insects are nutritious and totally normal food in many cultures. So next time you talk about insect eating, remember: 🧠 ‘Entomophagy’ is the academic word, ❤️ But maybe we just say ‘eating insects,’ like any other food! #bugible #entomophagy #insectivory

A lot of people want the farm life. Very few want to become skilled enough to build one. The truth is:Trades and agriculture go hand in hand. Welding.Diesel mechanics.Heavy equipment.Electrical work.Irrigation. These skills can save you thousands while creating income at the same time. A trade can fund the farm while the farm grows. Which skilled trade do you think is most valuable in agriculture?

Agriculture is changing fast. From rising beef prices and bird flu concerns to the New World screwworm moving closer to Texas, farmers and ranchers are being forced to stay informed now more than ever. The people who survive in agriculture aren’t always the biggest. They’re the ones who adapt the fastest. Stay alert. Study the market. Protect your operation. Move with strategy. Which issue do you think will impact agriculture the most this year? 👇

One of the biggest mistakes people make in agriculture is thinking farming alone will immediately fund the vision. The people who become dangerous in agriculture long-term usually develop skills beyond farming itself. Welding. Equipment operation. Diesel repair. Electrical work. Irrigation. Construction. Those skills create independence. They help you: • save money • build faster • reduce dependency • create additional income streams • keep the operation moving during hard seasons A skilled trade can literally fund the farm while the farm grows. That’s a powerful position to be in.

Most people are looking for land before they’re financially or strategically prepared for it. The truth is this: Buying farm land is not just about motivation. It’s about positioning. You need to understand: • loans • grants • infrastructure • income potential • zoning • water access • repayment ability • long-term strategy A lot of people think grants will buy them a farm. Most grants are actually designed to help improve operations after the land is secured. That’s why preparation matters. In this video, I break down the real steps to getting land and how people are actually using loans, grants, and strategy to build farm ownership. If you’re serious about buying land or starting a farm, this will help you avoid a lot of costly mistakes. A lot of people love the idea of farming. Very few are prepared for what it actually takes to build one. Because wanting a farm and building a farm are two completely different things. The dream is easy. The planning, budgeting, infrastructure, cash flow, and execution is what separates dreamers from operators. You do not need perfect land or massive acreage to start. But you do need structure, consistency, and a real strategy. If you are serious about building a profitable farm operation instead of just talking about “one day,” this is for you. The New World Screwworm is not just a “south of the border” problem anymore. It’s slowly moving north and Texas livestock producers, ranchers, pet owners, and wildlife managers need to be paying attention. This parasite attacks open wounds and can severely damage cattle, wildlife, pets, and even humans in rare cases. The earlier we spread awareness, the better prepared we are to protect our herds and operations. This is exactly why biosecurity, wound management, herd checks, and staying informed matter more than ever in modern agriculture. Texas is not immune. Stay alert. Protect what matters. APC PRESIDENTIAL PRIMARY: TINUBU GETS A LANDSLIDE VICTORY IN NIGER STATE. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has secured an overwhelming victory at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential primary held across the 25 local government areas of Niger State. Farmer Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago, who served as the Niger State collation officer for the APC presidential primary election, presented the result at the collation centre in Abuja. The farmer governor said President Tinubu polled 175,487 votes against his sole contender Stanley Osifo, who had 5,248 votes. Speaking to journalists shortly after the presentation, the farmer governor described the result of the presidential election in Niger State as a clear reaffirmation of the love and confidence that party members in the state have in the Tinubu-led administration. He reassured the President that the APC Niger State will continue to stand by him and ensure the realisation of the Renewed Hope agenda. A lot of people want the farm life. Very few want to become skilled enough to build one. The truth is:Trades and agriculture go hand in hand. Welding.Diesel mechanics.Heavy equipment.Electrical work.Irrigation. These skills can save you thousands while creating income at the same time. A trade can fund the farm while the farm grows. Which skilled trade do you think is most valuable in agriculture?

Agriculture is changing fast. From rising beef prices and bird flu concerns to the New World screwworm moving closer to Texas, farmers and ranchers are being forced to stay informed now more than ever. The people who survive in agriculture aren’t always the biggest. They’re the ones who adapt the fastest. Stay alert. Study the market. Protect your operation. Move with strategy. Which issue do you think will impact agriculture the most this year? 👇

One of the biggest mistakes people make in agriculture is thinking farming alone will immediately fund the vision. The people who become dangerous in agriculture long-term usually develop skills beyond farming itself. Welding. Equipment operation. Diesel repair. Electrical work. Irrigation. Construction. Those skills create independence. They help you: • save money • build faster • reduce dependency • create additional income streams • keep the operation moving during hard seasons A skilled trade can literally fund the farm while the farm grows. That’s a powerful position to be in.

The New World Screwworm is not just a “south of the border” problem anymore. It’s slowly moving north and Texas livestock producers, ranchers, pet owners, and wildlife managers need to be paying attention. This parasite attacks open wounds and can severely damage cattle, wildlife, pets, and even humans in rare cases. The earlier we spread awareness, the better prepared we are to protect our herds and operations. This is exactly why biosecurity, wound management, herd checks, and staying informed matter more than ever in modern agriculture. Texas is not immune. Stay alert. Protect what matters. We didn’t always grow just one kind of potato. We tested russets, fingerlings, and specialty varieties - thinking variety would drive sales. But most of them weren’t worth the space or the labor. ❌ Russets had low price points and inconsistent sizing, which made pricing frustrating. ❌ Fingerlings confused customers. Many didn’t recognize them or know how to use them, so they were easy to pass by. ❌ Specialty varieties caught attention but rarely converted. They looked great, but they didn’t move. So we simplified—and switched to baby red potatoes. ✅ We sold them by the quart for $5, which made pricing clear and effortless. ✅ They were familiar, versatile, and instantly appealing, so customers grabbed them without hesitation. ✅ We could plant them closer together, leading to higher yields and better profit per bed. It wasn’t about growing the most interesting crop. It was about growing what sold, scaled, and supported a strong market business. As I reported this morning we now have eight genetic ecotypes across Australia confirmed. Recent genomic research just published has updated our understanding of Dingoes, identifying eight genetically distinct populations across Australia. This classification includes two newly described groups in northern and central Australia, alongside previously known lineages like the isolated K'gari population and the genetically unique Mallee dingoes of the Big Desert.   ​These eight genetic groups provide a more precise map than the five traditional ecotypes: ​Alpine (Eastern Highlands)   ​Desert (Central and Western) ​Tropical (Northern) ​Forest (Southeastern forests) ​Coastal (Sandy coastal regions) ​Mallee (Northwestern Victoria/South Australia)   ​Northern (Top End) ​Central (Arid interior)   ​This new data highlights that the vast majority of "wild dogs" are actually Dingoes and emphasises the need for regional management to protect the specific genetic diversity of each group.   Why the "Wild Dog" Label is a Myth 🚫 ​For too long, the term "wild dog" has been used as a convenient excuse for lethal control. But the science is in, and it’s time to give the truth a fighting chance. ​New research from the University of Adelaide confirms what we’ve known: Australia’s free-roaming canines are vastly more Dingo than domestic dog. Calling them "wild dogs" is not just inaccurate—it’s a barrier to conservation. ​ ​Most "wild dogs" are genetically Dingoes. We need to stop using ancestry as a "threshold of Dingo-ness" to justify culling. ​Regional Crises: Our Mallee Dingoes in Victoria’s Big Desert are facing a genetic diversity crisis. They don't need "management"; they need protection. ​Let’s stop the misinformation. The Dingo is a native apex predator, not a "pest."  ​The truth is: Wild dogs ARE Dingoes. Help us share the science. 🐾🐾 #Dingoes #wildlife #wildanimals #dingoesoftiktok #dingoesofaustralia

It's constantly on my mind and breaks my heart that Dingoes are still being blasted, baited, tracked down, howled out and hunted in the wild because they are mistakenly perceived to damage agriculture❗️ Killing Dingoes removes them from the critical weight ecosystem, allowing foxes and cats to continuously increase the rate of mammal extinction.... Mistakenly livestock production comes before Australia's native wildlife. Graziers need to get their heads around the basic fact that they introduced a foreign prey animal into a native predators environment. Knowing this, the onus is on them to adequately protect their stock animals without adversely effecting the natural environment from which they sustain a livelihood. That is adequate respect for the welfare of their animals, the land, and all of the native wildlife. Too long has the status quo of colonial conqueror 'beat the land into submission' mindset been tolerated. 😔 The persecution of the Dingo is a complex issue with a long history and strong opinions on both sides. For many farmers, particularly those in sheep and cattle grazing areas, Dingoes are seen as a significant threat to their livestock. They can prey on young or vulnerable animals, leading to economic losses. Shooting, baiting (with 1080 poison), tracking, and hunting – have been employed for decades to manage Dingo populations in agricultural areas. On the other hand, Dingoes are a native apex predator in Australia and play a crucial role in the ecosystem. Many people value their presence and we are concerned about the impact of control measures on their populations and the wider environment. The humaneness of some control methods, particularly poisoning and trapping, raises significant ethical concerns for many animal welfare advocates. The methods used to control Dingoes can cause significant pain, distress, and a prolonged death. Continuous control measures can fragment Dingo populations, disrupt their social structures, and potentially threaten their long-term survival in some areas. As an apex predator, Dingoes help regulate populations of other animals, including feral pests like foxes and cats. Removing them can have unintended negative consequences for the ecosystem. The extent of Dingo predation on livestock is overstated in many areas, and lethal control can even worsen the problem by disrupting Dingo groups and leading to inexperienced individuals preying more on livestock. Alternative, non-lethal methods of livestock protection are available and, in some cases, proving effective. The "Wild Dog" Label is used to deliberately obscure the fact that the animals being targeted are often pure Dingoes or close Dingo hybrids, a native species❗️ The legal status of Dingoes varies across Australian states and territories. In some areas, they are protected, while in others, they are classified as pests. In Victoria, Dingoes are a threatened native species in some areas, but control measures are permitted under certain conditions, particularly to protect livestock. There is a wide range of views on Dingo management among farmers, conservationists, scientists,  advocates with the general public being unaware. There is increasing awareness of the ecological role of Dingoes and a growing movement advocating for non-lethal methods of livestock protection and a more nuanced approach to Dingo management. The conflict between protecting agriculture and conserving native wildlife is a challenging one, and the methods used to manage Dingoes raises significant ethical and ecological questions. 🐾🐾 The "1080" Debate: While 1080 poison is devastating, many graziers argue it is their only "affordable" option. To change their minds, the conversation usually has to shift toward subsidising non-lethal alternatives (like guardian dogs or smart fencing) so the financial burden doesn't fall solely on the farmer.🐾🐾 #Dingoes #wildlife #wildanimals #dingoesoftiktok #dingoesofaustralia

Stop calling Dingoes, "wild dogs."  Most free-roaming canids in Australia are genetically pure Dingoes or high-content, yet the "wild dog" label is constantly used to justify mass culling and strip them of their status as a native species. ​We need to flip the script: Dingoes are apex predators, not pests, and they are vital to the health of our ecosystem. It is time to stop the rebranding of a national icon just to make eradication easier.🤬 Several high-impact genetic and genomic studies on Dingoes have been published recently (late 2025–2026), primarily focused on correcting the "hybrid myth" and establishing a baseline for the species' native identity using ancient DNA. ​The key recent findings. ​The Hybridization Reassessment: New research using genome-wide SNP arrays and palaeogenomes (ancient DNA) suggests that domestic dog ancestry in Dingoes has been significantly overestimated (Weeks et al., 2024). Most free-roaming Dingoes show very low levels of European dog introgression, typically under 20% (Scarsbrook et al., 2025). ​Colonial Impacts and Identity: A 2025 PNAS study used ancient Dingo genomes from the Nullarbor Plain as a pre-colonial baseline. It found that while some gene flow occurred (peaking between the 1960s and 1980s), Dingoes have maintained a distinct genetic identity and shifted their diets following European arrival due to changes in prey abundance (Souilmi et al., 2024; Scarsbrook et al., 2025). ​Evolutionary Distinctiveness: New evidence supports the classification of the Dingo as a separate species or subspecies (Canis dingo), meeting criteria for reproductive isolation, genetic distinctiveness, and a unique evolutionary path independent of domestic dogs (UNSW, 2025). ​Regional Genetic Structure: Recent mapping highlights fine-scale population structures, specifically noting the genetic isolation and vulnerability of Dingoes in the Big Desert and Wyperfeld regions of Victoria (ARI, 2026). ​References ​Weeks, A. Dingoes aren't a problem❗️ It's the graziers that won't try to coexist.  Coexistence is the Key. ​True livestock protection doesn't come from a trap; it comes from Predator Smart Farming. Moving toward non-lethal solutions like Livestock Guardian Dogs and exclusion fencing allows us to protect our livelihoods without destroying the keystone species that keeps our ecosystems healthy. ​Dingoes have been the law-holders of this land for over 11,000 years. It’s time we stop fighting nature and start working with it to ensure a balanced future for both our farms and the wild.🐾🐾 #Dingoes #wildlife #wildanimals #dingoesoftiktok #dingoesofaustralia

The Reality of Aerial Baiting. 🤬 ​Right now, racks of meat are being prepared across the landscape—thawed, dried, and injected with 1080 poison to be dropped from the sky. These "buffer zones" don't just target Dingoes; they dismantle the ecological balance of our bush and ignore 11,000 years of history. ​The Facts: ✅️ ️​Indiscriminate Killing: Aerial baiting cannot distinguish between a Dingo and other native wildlife. ✅️ ️​Ecological Chaos: Removing apex predators triggers a trophic cascade, leading to a surge in smaller pests and loss of biodiversity. ✅️️ ​A Better Way: Predator-smart farming—like the use of Maremma guardian dogs and exclusion fencing—proves we can protect livestock without 1080 poison. ​We need federal protection for our native Dingoes and a transition to non-lethal, humane management. It is time to end the era of landscape-scale poisoning.🤮 Aerial baiting is underway in full swing now and racks of meat like these are lying around the place. These are being thawed and partially dried....Later they'll be injected with poison and dropped along "approved" transects to kill Dingoes❗️😡🤬 The sight of these meat racks is a stark reminder of the methods still being prioritised in landscape management. Preparing large-scale baiting programs like this highlights a significant divide between traditional lethal control and the movement toward more modern, non-lethal agricultural integration. ​The logistics of these programs often involve extensive preparation to ensure the baits are "shelf-stable" before being dropped. ​Thawing and drying the meat is a standard precursor to injecting the toxins, ensuring the bait remains attractive to canids while being durable enough to survive the drop from an aircraft. These "approved" transects are designed to create a perimeter, but they often fail to account for the ecological ripple effects (trophic cascades) that occur when an apex predator (the Dingo) is removed from the system. ​ ​While aerial baiting remains "business as usual" in many jurisdictions, there is a growing body of evidence supporting alternatives that protect both livestock and the integrity of the ecosystem: ​Livestock Guardian Dogs (LGDs): Using breeds like Maremmas or Anatolian Shepherds provides a 24/7 deterrent that doesn't rely on toxins. Advanced fencing and the use of "fright" tactics (lights, sound) can be highly effective at reducing conflict. ​ Many researchers argue that stable, socialised Dingo groups can actually regulate their own populations and territory, whereas indiscriminate killing leads to group breakdown and increased livestock predation by younger, inexperienced individuals. ​It is understandable why seeing these preparations is heartbreaking and so frustrating, especially when considering the 11,000-year history Dingoes  have on the continent. Moving away from 1080 and towards "predator-friendly" farming requires a massive shift in policy, but it's a conversation that is gaining momentum across Australia. 🙏🐾🐾 #Dingoes #wildlife #wildanimals #dingoesoftiktok #dingoesofaustralia

Alinta's beautiful thick, bushy tail.  While the primary function of their tail isn't solely for warmth, the fur does provide some insulation. It is also the alpine Dingoes' blanket during winter and females have larger heavier tails during puppy raising. Their tails are also important for balance and communication through body language. Dingoes possess a scent gland on their tail. This gland is located on the dorsal (upper) side of the tail, about one-quarter of the way down from the base. Dingoes use this scent gland for communication. They leave scent markings within their territory to signal their presence, mark boundaries, and potentially convey information about their reproductive status. They also use urine and feces for scent marking. So, while the thick, bushy tail contributes to their overall appearance and balance, the scent gland plays a specific and important role in their communication. 🐾🐾 #Dingoes #wildlife #wildanimals #dingoesoftiktok #dingoesofaustralia

AGRIGENS NEWS REPORT ON FUNAAB 27-28TH GLOBAL CONVENTION AND LECTURE SERIES.  The Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta Alumni Association has held its 28th–27th Annual Global Convention and Lecture Series, bringing together stakeholders to discuss national development and investment opportunities. Representing the Honourable Minister of Livestock Development, Idi Mukhtar Maiha, the Special Adviser on Knowledge Management and Communication, Dr Richard Mark Mbaram, stated that the establishment of the livestock ministry is capable of shaping Nigeria’s economic future. He said that the administration of Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains committed to transforming the livestock industry into a key driver of growth. Delivering the keynote lecture, Goke Adeyemi spoke on the theme “Mega Training  Approach to Creating Long-Term Business and Investment in an Evolving Economy.” He urged participants to prioritize research before committing funds to any venture, stressing that those who invest in knowledge and data-driven insights are more likely to succeed. Adeyemi noted that understanding market trends and economic shifts is critical, adding that “those who do the research ultimately own the business,” as informed decisions reduce risks and improve sustainability. The livestock ministry contributes to Nigeria's economy with plans to grow from the current $32billion to $74 billion within the next ten years driven by the livestock growth acceleration policy. Which focuses on improving productivity, strengthening value chain and encouraging investment in the sector. As part of the activities to mark this year global convention, the minister’s representative undertook an inspection tour of key facilities within FUNAAB. The visit included the university’s Alpha chicken, abattoir, and solar-powered engine room, where he commended the institution’s efforts in research, innovation, and sustainable agricultural practices. The event featured discussions on innovation, investment strategies, and the role of alumni networks in driving economic development, with participants encouraged to leverage knowledge, partnerships, and emerging opportunities for national growth. The 1926 Census has everyone talking this week, but what did it tell us about farming? At the time, over half of people at work were employed in agriculture. Farming wasn’t just an industry, it shaped everyday life across Ireland. Today,  fewer people work directly on farms, but agriculture still plays a central role in producing our food and supporting rural communities. It’s also worth noting that Census figures are based on a person’s main occupation, so they don’t fully capture part-time farming, something that’s still common across Ireland. In fact, the Central Statistics Office Census of Agriculture (2020) recorded 135,037 farms, highlighting the continued footprint of farming across the country. Diary of a Chicken Seller: Nigerian Must Go   A Message to Africa It is deeply unfortunate that we, as Africans, continue to find it difficult to live in peace with one another. A people who share the same soil, the same sun, the same ancestral blood  yet we raise our fists against each other like strangers. Recently, I came across a disturbing scene that broke my heart. A group of South African men, parading through the streets under the banner of what they called a "witch movement," were issuing loud warnings to all African foreigners  most especially Nigerians  to pack their bags and go back to their countries. The words "Nigerian Must Go" have once again echoed across South African streets, and the pain of it is too loud to ignore. As a writer, a thinker, and an African man who believes deeply in the idea of one Africa, I cannot keep silent. I have two messages to deliver today. First Message: To My South African Brothers and Sisters You cannot build a great nation alone while your brothers and sisters bleed in foreign lands. Africa's greatness has never been the story of one country  it has always been the collective strength of many peoples, many cultures, and many hands working together. The Nigerian in your street is not your enemy.  The Ghanaian, the Zimbabwean, the Congolese  none of them came to steal your future. Most came carrying dreams, skills, and a willingness to contribute. History will not be kind to a generation that chose division over unity. If South Africa rises, all Africa rises with it. If South Africa burns its bridges, it stands alone on an island of pride surrounded by a sea of regret. Choose unity. Choose brotherhood. Choose Africa. Second Message: To All African Foreigners in South Africa I know it is painful. I know the humiliation of being told to leave cuts deep especially when you have built a life, a business, a home, and a community in a place you came to love. But let me say this clearly: it is better to be alive and start again than to stay and die fighting for ground that was never yours to keep. Your life has more value than any property, any shop, or any investment. Pack with dignity. Pray with faith. And rebuild with the same spirit that made you leave home in the first place. The same God who gave you the courage to move the first time will give you the strength to rise again. We are Africans. We are resilient. We are builders. No "must go" can extinguish that fire. Diary of a Chicken Seller: Never Body Shame When the Loudest Critics Look Just Like You It is deeply unfortunate  and I mean this from the bottom of my chest  that the people most guilty of body shaming women are often women themselves. You did not design your body. You did not sit before creation and pick your shape, your curves, your chest size, or your stretch marks. That was God's doing. So if perfection is what you carry, take it up with the Creator  not with the woman standing next to you. I have always been the kind of person who, when everyone is facing one direction, turns deliberately to face another. That is just who I am. So while the Internet was busy reacting with outrage and theatrics over the Sis Alagbo situation, I was doing something different  I was drawing lessons. Let me be honest with you, as a street guy, I was not moved by what was in the tape itself. What moved me was the reaction of people. Think about it carefully. The moment something like that surfaces online, three things happen simultaneously. One you are inadvertently making that person more famous. Every share, every comment, every mocking story is free publicity. You are building the very person you claim to be tearing down.  Two  for every person screaming scandal, there are ten who secretly wish they had that kind of boldness, that kind of desire, that kind of life. People are performing outrage for the audience while privately admiring what they publicly condemn. Three  nobody was under pressure. Nobody was forced. Yet the same society that does worse behind closed walls wants to play saint in the comment section. What you do in private, my friend, is not always cleaner than what was exposed. The Body Shaming That Must Stop But the part that truly disturbed me  the part that kept me up  was a certain social media influencer who used this moment to mock the woman's body. Specifically, her breasts. Said they were not "slapping." Said they were flat. Said they had lost form. Let me ask you something: Did she make herself? Did she sit in heaven and request small breasts before descending to earth? Many women lose breast fullness after childbirth and breastfeeding. It is biology. It is sacrifice. It is what a woman's body does when it has nurtured life. And you  a woman yourself  want to stand on the Internet and shame her for it? That is not boldness. That is cruelty dressed in confidence. Every body is a story. Every sag, every scar, every stretch mark is evidence of living, of carrying children, of surviving. Diary of a Chicken Seller: We All Pray for a Better Nation, But Can We? It is deeply unfortunate that another election season is upon us  and with it comes the familiar cycle of wasteful spending, empty promises, and a political theatre most of us have watched one too many times.  Despite all the noise about clamping down on vote buying, some parties have already found smarter, more invisible ways to purchase loyalty  not with cash changing hands in the open, but through systems and structures designed to look clean on the surface. Now think about this carefully. When a man borrows money from a bank  or worse, from forces we may never see  just to secure a political seat, what exactly are you expecting when he finally arrives in power? He is not coming to serve. He is coming to recover.  Every contract awarded, every policy signed, every budget padded  all of it becomes a repayment plan for a debt the people never agreed to but will surely bear. Here is the hard truth we keep dancing around: we are not just victims of bad governance  many of us are participants in it. For the past three years, while the complaints have been loud, I want to ask a simple question  for those years when they were not sharing rice and oil at polling units, did you die? Did life stop? No, it did not. Yet some of us will still line up for a bag of semovita and a bottle of groundnut oil in exchange for our most powerful civic weapon  our vote. We trade the future for a meal that is finished before morning. And then there are the elites. The educated, the comfortable, the ones who speak loudest on social media about what is wrong with this country. I witnessed this firsthand during my service year the majority of those who actually showed up to vote were people who were told who to vote for.  They came in groups, directed like a movement. Meanwhile, the people with the knowledge, the awareness, and the platform to make a difference? Many of them did not even have voter cards. This is the irony that keeps recycling our suffering. So as this election season approaches, I want to speak plainly: if any party has failed you repeatedly, do not just complain  show up. Register. Get your voter card.  Participate in every activity that shapes the process. Because when we are all present, the conversation changes. When we are all watching, the manipulation becomes harder. If we stay home and stay silent, we have no right to complain about how the results are shared. Change does not fall from the sky. It is built, vote by vote, voice by voice, presence by presence. Diary of a Chicken Seller: We Blamed the Devil Too Much There is a habit deeply rooted in many of us  the moment something goes wrong, the devil gets the credit. We never stop to ask ourselves the harder question: what role did I play in this? Accepting your fault and claiming responsibility in every situation where you may have gone wrong is one of the most important things a person can do. Not occasionally. Not when it is convenient. Every. Single. Time. Because the alternative  pointing fingers at an invisible force is slowly destroying the fabric of our society. Think about it honestly.  Can the devil, without any human intervention, build a bridge? Can he design a road, erect a building, or run an institution? Of course not. Every structure we interact with daily was built by human hands, shaped by human decisions, and maintained by human choices. So then why is it that the moment those same human hands make a wrong turn  when ego takes the wheel, when greed clouds judgment, when laziness creeps in  the very first response is "it is the work of the devil"? If we truly believe, as many of us profess, that the devil cannot act without human cooperation, then submitting yourself to wrong impulses and later blaming him is nothing short of a contradiction. That contradiction, right there, is a refusal to take responsibility. And a person who will not take responsibility cannot grow. This problem does not stop at the individual level. Some of the most dangerous failures in our society trace back to people in positions of trust who refused to own their mistakes. Parents who abandoned their role and blamed spiritual forces instead of confronting their own shortcomings.  Leaders who drove communities into the ground and turned to superstition rather than accountability. The children of those decisions are still paying the price today. That is what an inherited problem looks like a wound passed down because someone upstream could not find the courage to say "I was wrong." If we can open our eyes, truly open them, we would see that accepting our faults is not weakness. It is the beginning of wisdom. It is how we stop adding to the burden of the next generation. It is how we break cycles that have been running for decades. Own your mistakes. Correct your path. Let the devil find someone else to blame. Mobile solar generator trailers are essentially "large mobile outdoor power banks" designed to provide off-grid energy without the noise or emissions of traditional diesel generators. How It Works: The Core Components A mobile solar generator integrates several key technologies into a single towable unit: Solar Array: Foldable monocrystalline silicon panels capture sunlight and convert it into electrical energy. These panels are often adjustable to follow the sun's latitude for maximum absorption. MPPT Charge Controller: A Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller regulates the voltage and current from the panels, ensuring the batteries charge with up to 95% efficiency while preventing overcharging. Energy Storage: The system uses deep-cycle batteries (typically gel or lithium-ion) to store power for use at night or during cloudy weather. Inverter System: To power standard tools and electronics, an inverter converts the stored DC battery power into AC power (110V/240V/380V), typically producing a "pure sine wave" for stable, safe operation of sensitive equipment. Key Features: Hybrid Charging: While solar is the primary source, these trailers can also be recharged via the city power grid if solar input is insufficient due to weather. Intelligent Management: Many units feature a Battery Management System (BMS) and remote monitoring capabilities (via Wi-Fi or GPRS), allowing users to track power levels and operating temperatures in real-time on a PC or mobile device. Rugged Mobility: Designed for extreme environments, these trailers are built with hot-dip galvanized steel, can withstand winds up to 117 km/h (Level 8), and are IP65 rated for weather protection. Primary Applications These units are used across various sectors where reliable, off-grid power is critical: Emergency & Disaster Relief: Providing immediate power for medical tents, communications, and lighting in areas where the grid has failed. Construction & Mining: Powering tools, site offices, and high-efficiency LED lighting towers for night shifts. Remote Surveillance: Supporting "smart" camera systems with AI analysis for site security in off-grid locations. Outdoor Events & Film Production: Offering silent, emission-free power that won't interfere with audio recording or guest experiences.

Did you know this? 🍹 Most people think the Spritz started with Aperol. Not exactly. 🇮🇹🍹 The Spritz was born in the region of Veneto and became part of local aperitivo culture long before it became famous around the world. While Aperol Spritz is now the most popular version internationally, many Venetians consider a Spritz made with Select to be the traditional Venetian version. Created in Venice in 1920, Select became closely associated with the city’s aperitivo culture and is still used today in many historic Venetian bars. Of course, there isn’t just one way to make a Spritz. Depending on where you are in Veneto, you may find it made with Select, Aperol, Campari, or other bitters. But if you want to experience a classic Venetian Spritz, many locals will tell you to reach for Select 🇮🇹🍹

Have you ever had this dish? 🍝  Why is it called Spaghetti alla Puttanesca? 🇮🇹🍝 Spaghetti alla Puttanesca is a classic pasta from southern Italy made with tomatoes, olives, capers, garlic, and often anchovies. Its origin is still debated. One popular legend says the dish was prepared in the brothels of Naples because it was quick to make and used simple pantry ingredients. Another theory is that the name was simply a colorful way of describing a pasta made with whatever was available. The first documented references to puttanesca don’t appear until around the 1950s, which is why the true story remains uncertain.

Did you know this? 🤔  Did you know many Sicilian foods have Arabic roots? 🇮🇹🌍 The Arab presence in Sicily between the 9th and 11th centuries left a lasting impact on the island’s culture, agriculture, language, and food. In fact, dozens of Sicilian food-related words are believed to come from Arabic. The Arab influence also introduced or helped spread ingredients that are now closely associated with Sicilian cuisine, including citrus fruits, sugar cane, almonds, pistachios, and many irrigation techniques that transformed the island’s agriculture. It’s one of the reasons Sicilian food is so unique — a blend of influences from the many civilizations that have called the island home over the centuries.

Who wants a piece? 🙋🏻‍♂️ One of Italy’s hidden food gems 🇮🇹🧀 Focaccia di Recco IGP comes from the town of Recco in Liguria, near Genoa. Unlike regular focaccia, this version is made with two very thin layers of dough filled with soft, creamy cheese — traditionally Stracchino. It’s baked at a very high temperature until crispy on the outside and melted inside 🤤 Focaccia di Recco also has an IGP certification, meaning it’s closely tied to its geographic area and traditional way of being made. Simple ingredients, but an incredible food tradition 🇮🇹

Have you noticed it? 🧀  Those white spots on Parmigiano Reggiano are not mold 🇮🇹🧀 They’re actually called tyrosine crystals — small crunchy crystals that naturally form as the cheese ages. Tyrosine is an amino acid found in milk proteins. Over time, as aged cheeses mature and their proteins slowly break down, the tyrosine begins to crystallize, creating those little white spots. They’re often considered a sign of proper aging and quality, especially in long-aged cheeses. And Parmigiano Reggiano isn’t the only cheese where this happens. You can also find tyrosine crystals in other aged cheeses like: ✅ Grana Padano ✅ Pecorino Romano ✅ aged cheddars ✅ gouda ✅ alpine-style cheeses So if you see these little crunchy spots on properly aged cheese… that’s usually a very good sign

Would you eat it like an apple? This onion is famous for being incredibly sweet 🇮🇹🧅 Cipolla Rossa di Tropea Calabria PGI is a traditional red onion from the region of Calabria in southern Italy. Thanks to the area’s climate, soil, and proximity to the sea, these onions develop a much sweeter and milder flavor than typical onions — so much so that many people in Italy eat them raw in salads, sandwiches, or even bite into them like an apple. The onion also holds a PGI (Protected Geographical Indication) certification, meaning it is closely tied to its geographic area and must follow specific production standards. It’s another perfect example of how Italy protects regional foods deeply connected to local tradition and terroir 🇮🇹

Spoiler: no horses involved 🇮🇹 🐴  One of Italy’s oldest cheeses 🇮🇹 Caciocavallo is a traditional cheese from southern Italy, especially regions like Molise and Abruzzo. Its name is believed to come from the way the cheeses are tied together and hung a cavallo (“on horseback”) over wooden beams while they age. The result is a rich, savory cheese that becomes sharper and more complex over time. 👉 This is one of the experiences we’ll have on my trip to Abruzzo and Molise in July 2026 — stepping inside real cheese aging rooms and experiencing a side of Italy most travelers never see 🇮🇹 💬 Message me if you want details on the trip 👀

You prob know my opinion 😅  I noticed that on some Giovanni Rana packaging here in the United States, gnocchi are suggested as a side dish to meat. That caught my attention because in Italy, Gnocchi are traditionally considered a primo piatto (first course), similar to pasta or risotto — not typically a side dish. Of course, food culture can evolve and adapt depending on the country and market, and there’s nothing wrong with people enjoying food however they like. But I do think it raises an interesting conversation about how traditional Italian dishes are interpreted outside of Italy — even by Italian brands themselves.

Could you see yourself here? 🇮🇹 This July, I’m taking a small group to Abruzzo and Molise — regions where traditions are still alive, villages feel frozen in time, and food is deeply connected to culture and community. We’ll experience things most travelers never do: dining on a trabocco above the Adriatic Sea, stepping inside cheese aging rooms, cooking in a real Italian home, exploring hidden villages, and experiencing a slower, more authentic side of Italy. This isn’t just a vacation. It’s a completely different way to experience Italy. 📆 July 19-28, 2026 👥 Small group experience ⚠️ Only a few spots left 💬 Message me for the itinerary and details 👀

What are your thoughts? 🍅  A new lawsuit filed in California accuses Cento Fine Foods of misleading consumers over its “Certified San Marzano” tomatoes. The lawsuit claims many consumers believed the tomatoes were officially certified as true PDO San Marzano tomatoes from Italy, while the certification referenced on the cans comes from a separate third-party certifier rather than the official consortium protecting Pomodoro San Marzano dell’Agro Sarnese-Nocerino DOP. Cento has denied the allegations and has called the lawsuit meritless.  This story highlights something very important: understanding labels like PDO and PGI on Italian products. In Italy, PDO certifications are tied to strict geographic and production rules designed to protect authenticity and origin. However, these protections do not operate in the United States the same way they do in Europe. So the issue raised in the lawsuit isn’t necessarily whether the tomatoes are good or bad — it’s whether consumers clearly understood what they were buying.

Mission accomplished. We wrapped up our nationwide tour in CRR and LRR by laying foundation stones for vital road infrastructure in Niamina. Today, we laid foundation stones to build over 49 kilometers of new roads across four local communities: Jarumeh Koto–Manna–Salikenen, Wassu Junction–Kuntaur–Jakaba–Niani Sukuta–Barajally Tenda, Nyagabantang–Bakadaji, and the Wassu–Kataba Omar Ndow–Kataba Seringe roads.

Better roads mean better access to health, education, and economic opportunities for all Gambians.  #PresidentBarrow #TheGambia #Infrastructure #NationalDevelopment 🇬🇲

True national development means connecting production directly to prosperity. Guided by our Yiriwaa Plan, these new roads will cut transportation hardships, raise farming incomes, improve healthcare access, and foster seamless regional trade.  Thank you to the vibrant communities of URR and CRR for the warm, humbling welcome. Together, we build our nation.

Seed quantity is one of the most important factors when growing with aeroponic towers. Some crops, like lettuce, only require one seed per hole in order to form proper heads without competing for space with neighboring plants. But herbs like thyme can require up to 10 seeds per hole to produce full harvests. Over the years, we’ve carefully dialed in the ideal seed quantity for every crop we grow, maximizing yields on the towers while avoiding overcrowding. Too few seeds creates sparse harvests. Too many seeds causes the plants to compete. The goal is finding the perfect balance. #seeds #farming #plants #gardening #agriculture

This is how we grow 40 cucumber plants on 4 aeroponic towers. 1. Planting Strategy: We skip the bottom growing level on each aeroponic tower and transplant no more than 1 cucumber seedling per level on opposing sides. Cucumbers grow very large with long sprawling vines, so limiting the number of plants improves airflow, light exposure, plant health, and overall yields. Across 4 towers, this gives us a total of 40 cucumber plants. 2. Grow Cage: We use a custom-built grow cage made from galvanized steel specifically designed for climbing crops like cucumbers. The structure uses attachable horizontal metal cables which the cucumber tendrils naturally latch onto as they grow. This allows the plants to spread both vertically and horizontally throughout the cage, providing better support and more growing space. 3. Seedlings: Cucumbers germinate and grow extremely quickly. We place only one seed per Rockwool cube to avoid root competition later on. Rockwool is a sterile soilless growing medium made from basaltic rock with an excellent air-to-water ratio for hydroponic and aeroponic growing. 4. Nutrient Delivery: Inside the aeroponic towers, the roots are intermittently irrigated with nutrient-enriched water containing all essential macronutrients and trace minerals required for healthy cucumber growth. Because the roots receive high oxygen exposure, the plants can grow exceptionally fast. 5. Pest Management: One of the biggest pest issues we encounter with cucumbers is aphids, which can also spread mosaic viruses such as Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV). To control them, we mainly use neem oil extracted from the neem tree, along with agricultural soap which helps break down soft-bodied insects like aphids. Both are commonly used in organic agriculture. 6. Cucumber Varieties: The cucumber varieties shown in this video include Unagi, Marketmore, Diva, and Salt & Pepper cucumbers. 7. Harvest: Cucumbers must be harvested regularly to encourage continuous fruit production throughout the growing cycle. #cucumber #farming #agriculture #horticulture #gardening

This is how we grow 18 cabbages vertically on aeroponic towers.  1. Rockwool: This soilless growing substrate is made from basaltic rock that is melted and spun into fibers. In its dry form, it naturally has a high pH, so we first soak it in reverse osmosis water adjusted to a pH of around 5.5–6.0, which is ideal for seed germination. 2. Cabbage Seeds: It’s extremely important not to sow more than one cabbage seed per cube in order to avoid overcrowding and competition between the plants later on. 3. Vermiculite: This is a naturally occurring mineral that expands when heated. It has an excellent air-to-water ratio, helps keep the seeds in place, improves moisture retention for germination, and is chemically inert, meaning it does not significantly react with or alter the nutrient solution. 4. Seedlings: After about three weeks, the seedlings should have 2–4 true leaves before being transplanted into the towers. 5. Transplanting: We never transplant more than two cabbage seedlings per growing port in order to provide enough space for the cabbages to properly develop and reach their full size. 6. Pest Management: The main pest affecting our cabbages are cabbage worms. During the first month of growth, we apply Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) once per week, a naturally occurring beneficial bacteria approved for organic farming. Bt specifically targets caterpillars when they feed on the leaves, helping protect the crop without harming beneficial insects, humans, or the plants themselves. 7. Growth Cycle: The cabbages are automatically irrigated inside the towers with nutrient-enriched water containing all essential macronutrients and trace elements needed for healthy growth. 8. Harvest: Once the cabbages are ready for harvest, we remove the outer cabbage leaves before harvesting the heads. These leaves are also completely edible and we use them either raw or cooked. #cabbage #farming #agriculture #vegetable #gardening

Spring onions take around 8 weeks to reach their ideal harvest size from the day the seedlings are transplanted. They’re relatively slow-growing, but very low-maintenance crops. While spring onions grow well on aeroponic towers, traditional onions don’t because they form underground bulbs. The same applies to potatoes, carrots, and most root vegetables or tubers. #springonions #greenonions #scallions #farming #agriculture

This soilless farming method works equally well for all kinds of herbs including basil, cilantro, mint, dill, thyme, sage, oregano, marjoram, tarragon, and many more. Using the right number of seeds per growing port is essential for producing full, healthy herb bunches while avoiding overcrowding and maximizing yields. #parsley #herbs #farming #gardening #agriculture

This method of farming allows you to grow far more crops in a fraction of the space while using up to 95% less water than traditional agriculture. By growing vertically on aeroponic towers, you can produce over 160 different crops, including leafy greens, herbs, vegetables, fruits, and even flowers. Everything is grown without soil, with roots suspended in air and fed with a perfectly balanced nutrient solution. Each plant receives exactly what it needs, when it needs it, resulting in faster growth, higher yields, and consistent quality. #farming #gardening #agriculture #aeroponics #hydroponics

This is how we maximize parsley production. On a single aeroponic tower, we can grow up to 8 kilos of parsley in less than one square meter. From seed to seedling takes about 3 weeks, followed by around 6 weeks from transplant to harvest. We recommend sowing 6 seeds per growing port to produce full, well-sized bunches without overcrowding, allowing for an efficient use of space while maintaining high-quality yields. #parsley #herbs #farming #gardening #agriculture

Growing dill on aeroponic towers is all about choosing the right variety. Instead of traditional dill, which can grow up to 1.5 meters tall, we go for compact varieties like Teddy or Thalia. These stay low and bushy, usually around 30–50 cm, making them ideal for vertical systems where space efficiency matters. To really maximize production, we sow five seeds per port. This gives us full, dense bunches and helps us get the most out of every tower. From transplant to harvest, dill is fast, ready in about six weeks, allowing us to produce up to 450 bunches of dill per year on a single tower.  #dill #farming #agriculture #gardening #horticulture

Spider mites are one of the most brutal pests to manage in greenhouse farming. Many farmers underestimate them… until they wipe out an entire production cycle. The major problem in Nigeria is that we have very limited active ingredients that truly disrupt the spider mite life cycle effectively. Most farmers rely heavily on Abamectin. While products like Cypermethrin and Neem oil are commonly mentioned, their field performance against heavy infestations is often inconsistent. Neem oil can help, yes… but not at the level required for aggressive greenhouse pressure. Unfortunately, years of Abamectin abuse and underdosing by many farmers have pushed spider mites toward resistance. Recently, we introduced a combination of Fenpyroximate + Hexythiazox into our rotation strategy and the reduction in mite pressure has been significant. We also alternate with Hirsutella thompsonii (biological control agent), Karanjin extract (a botanical) and Methomyl.  We sell the botanical and biological. Spider mite management is no longer about “spraying anything”. It is now a game of resistance management, life cycle disruption and intelligent rotation. If we were not extremely aggressive and disciplined with pest management, some of our greenhouse units would have crashed completely. In my opinion, spider mites are worse than thrips. Once they establish properly inside a greenhouse, they become a nightmare for every farmer. Do you want to farm like a serious grower instead of gambling with your crops? Correct tail setting isn’t just about looks — it’s a functional trait. A low, straight tail head indicates correct pelvic structure, which means easier calving and fewer problems for your cows. A twisted “wry tail” at the tail head is a serious fault to cull, as it can be linked to spinal issues. Selecting for good tail set helps you breed sound, fertile females that stay productive longer. #agriculture  #livestock  #agritips  #agriculture  #fyp

When we experience excessive rainfall, it washes water soluble nutrients like nitrogen, potassium, calcium and magnesium from grass roots and deeper into the soil where plants can't reach them. This makes the grasses less nutritious, less palatable with less protein and more tough fiber. As a result, animals get poorer quality grazing, and they often hammer the few good grasses that are left (selective grazing). Additional supplementation is essential will assist our livestock to get access to nutrient that are unavailable in the veld. #fyp #veldmangement #agriculture #livestock

Severely overgrazed veld takes 10–30+ years to recover naturally in semi-arid areas. There are studies that show grasses which only returned after four good rain years, even with grazing cut by two-thirds. Reseeding perennials and strict rest can shorten it to 5–15 years but it's a costly and intensive process with no guarantee especially with unpredictable weather conditions.  Prevention is cheaper than repair. 🌾 Check comment archon for a pluk 😉👍🏽   #fyp  #farming  #grazing  #agriculture  #agriculturesouthafrica

Effective veld management is crucial, involving practices like rotational grazing is crucial to maintain ecosystem health and prevent degradation. Rainfall patterns significantly impact veld productivity, with different veld types such as sweetveld, sourveld, grassveld, and bushveld requiring tailored management approaches. Understanding these factors is key to sustainable land use and biodiversity conservation. #fyp #agriculture #veld #animals #farmlife
